RIGIDITY AT EXPECTED COST m:
Fix anyP. A universal algorithm with totalmean<=m for everyQ has EN_Q=m andEN_P=0 bythe stopped-KL floor. For anypositiveQ,Q0, transcriptKL=(EN_Q)D(Q||Q0)=mD(Q||Q0)=outputKL. Equality in finite-output data processing says each finite stopped transcript's likelihood ratio is the ratio of its outputY word. Source/fairbit/oldP factors cancel, so
 product_i(q_i/q0_i)^[n_i(transcript)-count_i(Y)]=1.
Use a countable dense collection ofpositiveQ and equivalence toQ0 to choose a common probability-one transcript set; continuity and varying eachq_i toward0 force every exponentzero. Therefore EXACTLYmQ replies occur a.s. and their empiricalhistogram equalsY's histogram, despite initially allowing adaptive unbounded stopping. ExtraP replies costzeroa.s. No probability oracle or hardcap premise is introduced by this conclusion.
Pathwise same-row mismatch is then at leastTV(empX,empZ) for the actualfirstmQ replies. AtP=Quniform its expectation is at leastdelta_(d,m). Thus no actual m-cost algorithm can meeteta<delta.

INFIMUM/NONATTAINMENT IS ALSO PAID:
IfC*=m were approached only byalgorithms ofworstmeansm+1/n, collapse each finite algorithm's internal fairbit computation into data-independent stochastic next-action probabilities at each finite visible history/oldword (nextPcall/Qcall/or terminalY). There are countably many histories, finite action sets, finite old/output words. Compactness/diagonal subsequence gives a limitpolicy. Uniform Markov tailP(N>K)<=(m+1)/(K+1) gives a.s.finitequerytermination for everyP,Q; finite-cylinder probabilities converge. Fatou gives limitmean<=m. The sameuniformtail and boundedfiniteoutput/mismatch preserve exactQ^m and the retention inequality. This limit may use noncomputable transition probabilities; it is ONLY a relaxed-class lower-bound device, not an emittedalgorithm/free-real oracle. The stopped-KL/likelihood-ratio argument applies to such a universal stochasticpolicy aswell and forces the same histogram rigidity. Hence eta<delta also rules out an infimum m. The computable histogram algorithm attains m ontheother side, so the IFF covers the actual C* rather than assumingattainment.

DEFINE exact rational
 delta_(d,m)=d/(2m)*E|A-B|, A,B independent Bin(m,1/d).
THEOREM: C*(d,m,eta)=m IFF eta>=delta_(d,m). This characterizes the entire information-minimum regime, not all values above that floor.

UPPER/WORST-CASE EMPIRICAL EXCESS:
The accepted permutation-equivariant original-row histogram matcher uses exactlymQ/noP and gives entireQ^m, with changedfractionTV(empX,empZ). Set g_m(p,q)=E|Bin(m,p)-Bin'(m,q)|-m|p-q|. Ifp>=q, g=2E[(B-A)+]; monotone binomial coupling in either argument gives g(p,q)<=min{h_m(p),h_m(q)}, h_m(p)=E|Bin(m,p)-Bin'(m,p)|. Same bysymmetry otherwise. Thus for everyP,Q empiricalexcess<=sum_i h_m(p_i)/(2m).
Putu=p(1-p). The integer absolute-value Fourier identity gives
 h_m(p)=(1/pi)*integral_0^pi [1-(1-2u*(1-cos t))^m]/(1-cos t) dt.
For0<=u<=1/4 each integrand is increasing and concave inu (m1 islinear); at t0 use the continuous limit. Composition with concavep(1-p) makes h_m concave inp. Jensen gives sum_i h_m(p_i)<=d*h_m(1/d). Equality occurs atP=Q=uniform[d]. Consequently the EXACT supremum overP,Q of ETV(empX,empZ)-TV(P,Q) is delta_(d,m), not merely a fluctuation upper bound. This proves the theorem's sufficiency with the existing exactjoint matcher, expected finite integer-tie bits/local work and paid oldinput/storage/output.
